correctness.rationale: For each m>=2, Faulhaber prime-power restriction F_{m,p}(X) has exact X^{1 or 2} times H_{m,p}, with degree 2 floor(m/2), nonzero Bernoulli constant and leading coefficient (p-1)/(p(m+1)). Choose p>k+2 avoiding fixed Bernoulli numerators; p H_{m,p} is Eisenstein at p for both s,k, so each H irreducible. If integer P(p^u)|Q(p^u) for all u, polynomial division Q=PA+R, clearing denominators, makes M R(p^u)/P(p^u) an integer tending to zero, forcing R=0. For k>s, H_s|H_k would force association; degrees differ except even s,k=s+1, where leading and constant ratios (s+1)/(s+2) versus (s+1)/2 disagree. For reverse distinct s>k>=2, n=3 yields phi_s(3)>phi_k(3). The proof establishes all s>=2, not just finite verifier ranges.
residual_risks: Any included finite computations are corroboration only; the universal conclusions rest on the reconstructed proofs.
